name: Oriented PPTA high-strength fiber
summary: A very strong, light synthetic fibre spun from a liquid-crystal polymer solution, best known as Kevlar, which was soon woven into bullet-resistant body armour.
description: Poly(p-phenylene terephthalamide) is processed from a nematic solution into highly oriented aromatic-polyamide fibers.

why: DuPont was searching for a light, very strong fibre, initially with tyre reinforcement in mind.

events.statement: A Hexcel Schwebel manager recalled that the company began weaving Kevlar fabric for body armor in 1972.
events.scope: DuPont PPTA fiber woven by Hexcel Schwebel into fabric intended for body armor.
events.caveats: The 1972 date is a retrospective company interview, without a specific invoice. A 1994 NRC chapter says commercialization occurred in 1970, while a DuPont representative dates introduction to 1972; other histories date early production to the early 1970s. The separate Soviet Vniivlon high-strength fiber was reported in 1969 and 1971; no worldwide first or superiority over it is asserted.
